headline: High-altitude florist discovers that marigolds grown at 10,600 feet develop an annoying superiority complex
body:
Local gardener Tenzin Dorje, who oversees the newly unveiled twin floral fields in Leh, reported today that the high-altitude blossoms have begun to refuse growth near common, sea-level marigolds. According to Dorje, the flowers, thriving in the oxygen-depleted thin air, have started displaying 'elitist' behavior, including curling their petals at visitors who arrive at the site by bus instead of via arduous multi-day trek.

'It’s quite difficult to manage a garden where the blooms look down on you,' said Dorje, while attempting to prune a particularly snooty batch of petunias. 'These flowers have developed a very specific aura of Himalayan exclusivity. If you try to compare them to anything grown in the plains, they simply wilt in a way that suggests you lack refined horticultural taste. One rosebud yesterday refused to bloom until I played a recording of wind chimes vibrating at exactly 4,000 Hertz.'

Botanists believe the phenomenon is a natural evolutionary response to being officially designated as the 'highest' in the world. The flowers have reportedly requested that their watering schedule be moved to 'peak golden hour' to better match their status as high-altitude influencers. Dorje notes that the floral fields have already started a waiting list for bees, strictly prohibiting entry to any insect that has recently visited a lower-elevation garden.
caption: Local flowers in Leh have officially reached peak snobbery after growing at 10,600ft. Would you trek up a mountain just to be judged by a petunia? #LehFlowers #HimalayanGardens #FlowerPower #GardeningDrama (satire)
